claims: The Artemis II reentry was on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II reentry featured a 24,000 mph, 5,000-degree fireball.
The Artemis II reentry passed over the Pacific at roughly 5:07 p.m. PDT.
Sonic booms were possible during the Artemis II reentry.
The Artemis II splashdown was scheduled for approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT) on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II splashdown zone was situated roughly 70 miles south of Newport Harbor, near the east end of San Clemente Island.
Officials cautioned that low clouds and the distance meant the Artemis II re-entry firestreak might not be visible from beaches or land.
NASA provided a live, high-definition stream of the re-entry, descent, and splashdown on NASA+, the NASA App, and NASA's YouTube Channel.
The Artemis II crew piloted the Orion capsule.
The Artemis II crew underwent a "skip reentry".
The "skip reentry" managed the intense heat of returning from the Moon.
